plan: With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the symmetric Nash equilibrium bidding strategy in a first-price auction is to bid (n-1)/n of your value, which accounts for the number of competitors. With n=3, this means bidding 2/3 of my value. My value is $36, so optimal bid = 2/3 * 36 = $24. This balances winning probability against profit margin, maximizing expected profit given uncertainty about others' values.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the standard symmetric equilibrium bid shading factor for a first-price auction is (n-1)/n = 2/3. My value is $33, so I'll bid approximately 33 * (2/3) ≈ 22 to balance winning probability against overpaying, maximizing expected profit given rational competitors likely bidding similarly.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction strategy is to shade my bid to (n-1)/n of my value, which is 2/3 for n=3. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $31, so I calculate 31 * (2/3) ≈ 20.7. Bidding this amount maximizes expected profit given the equilibrium strategy assuming other bidders behave similarly rationally.
